..
Issued at 302 AM EDT Wed Oct 7 2026

Today-Tonight...Ongoing light to moderate showers near and north of 
I-4 are forecast to persist through daybreak, as a front remains 
stalled across the local forecast area. Little change overall 
forecast today compared to yesterday, with high coverage of showers 
once again expected. 

Multiple rounds of showers and embedded lightning storms will 
traverse the area today, fueled by lift along the stationary front 
and deep moisture (PWATs 2.2-2.4"). This will lead to PoPs 80-90% 
area- wide. Low instability due to dense cloud cover from early 
showers will likely suppress the deepest convection and most 
lightning strikes across the northern half of the area today, though 
can't rule out a strike or two. Instead, drier conditions this 
morning across the southern half of the CWA is forecast to provide 
enough breaks in the (still dense) cloud cover for more efficient 
daytime heating. This will create the best chance for scattered 
lightning strikes and deeper convection, supported by the most 
recent CAM runs. Widespread rainfall totals near 2" are expected 
today within rounds of showers and storms. However, isolated totals 
near 4" cannot be ruled out embedded within deeper convection, 
likely across southern portions of the area. Regardless, all of east 
central Florida has been highlighted in a Marginal Risk (1/4) for 
excessive rainfall. Minor flooding will be possible, exacerbated in 
areas that have already seen heavy rainfall the last several days. A 
gust to 45 mph cannot be ruled out across the south in the strongest 
storms.

Showers and a few storms will persist through this evening and into 
tonight, especially north of the front. Thus, rainfall accumulations 
look to persist, though rainfall rates will be lower with a lack of 
deep convection. Models have backed off on the strength of the 
surface low forecast to develop just offshore.
Therefore, forecast wind speeds this afternoon have diminished.
Light and variable flow this morning becomes NE into tonight, but 
remains around 10 mph or less. Dense cloud cover looks to keep high 
temperatures in the upper 70s to lower 80s north of Melbourne, with 
breaks in the clouds allowing areas to the south to warm into the 
upper 80s. Humid conditions will support heat indices in the upper 
90s to near 100 in the warmest areas.

Thursday-Friday...The stationary front is forecast to remain 
generally stalled across the local area through late week. 
Meanwhile, the Atlantic ridge nudges westward through the period, 
beginning to steer TD 9 northward, well west of east central 
Florida. A bit of rinse and repeat forecast for Thursday, as deep 
moisture maintains high PoPs (70-80%) across the peninsula. Multiple 
rounds of showers and embedded storms are expected to once again 
produce widespread, additional rainfall accumulations of 2", with 
pockets of 4" possible. Once again, the greatest chance for 
lightning strikes and deeper convection looks to be across southern 
portions of the area. By Friday, the front is expected to begin to 
slowly lift northward, reducing accumulations to around 1-2". 
However, PoPs remain around 70-80%.
Will need to monitor the threat for a few spin ups Friday afternoon 
into Friday night, as 850 mb winds begin to veer.

The pressure gradient tightens slightly late week, as TD 9 
strengthens. But, onshore flow is forecast to remain around 10-15 
mph or less. High temperatures creep up a degree or two each day 
from south to north, as cloud cover decreases slightly. Highs return 
to the mid to upper 80s by Friday. Continued humid conditions will 
lead to heat indices in the lower 100s across the south late week.

Saturday-Wednesday...Upper level ridging over the western Atlantic 
is forecast to help steer what is currently TD 9 into the northern 
Gulf coast by Saturday. Models are in fairly good agreement that the 
ridge is nudged southward by a passing trough and flattened across 
the southern Florida peninsula late weekend, before stacking and 
strengthening over the northwestern Gulf early next week. Locally, 
high coverage of showers and storms continues Saturday, as the 
stalled front finally lifts northward on the eastern periphery of TD 
9. Strengthening southerly flow between the ridge and TD 9 will 
continue to advect deep moisture into the peninsula, supporting PoPs 
up to 60-80% through this weekend. Breezy and gusty conditions are 
forecast, especially on Saturday along the coast, making for poor to 
hazardous beach and boating conditions. As the ridge strengthens 
over the Gulf, lighter northerly winds develop into next week, 
finally reducing PWATs and putting an end to the above normal 
coverage of showers and storms. In fact, could see mostly dry 
conditions by midweek, but the forecast maintains 20-30% PoPs for 
now. High temperatures look to increase and linger in the upper 80s 
through the period, though nearer to normal lows are possible next 
week.
